metas.name: Albania - Cylinder Water Tanks
metas.note:
• You will see a lot of cylinder-shaped water tanks on the roofs of buildings.

--- NOTE:

  • This is less common in Montenegro.
  • Some parts of Turkey also have a lot of similar-looking water tanks.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/albania for more clues.

metas.name: Andorra - Stone Buildings
metas.note:
• Andorra has a lot of these stone buildings.
  • They can be seen almost everywhere in the country.

--- NOTE:

  • These buildings can also be found close to Andorra, in the French and Spanish Pyrenees.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/andorra for more clues.

metas.name: Belgium - Red Bricks
metas.note:
• A lot of houses in Belgium are made of distinctive red bricks.

--- NOTE:

  • This is more common in the North and West of the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/belgium for more clues.

metas.name: Belgium - South - Gray Tone Stones
metas.note: • Houses in the South of the country use a lot of stone, have gray tones and generally look more French.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/belgium for more clues.

metas.name: Bhutan - Unique Architecture
metas.note:
• The traditional Bhutanese architecture is very distinct.
  • Most of the houses have tin roofs and wooden painted frames, which give them a unique look.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bhutan for more clues.

metas.name: Bolivia - Unfinished Look
metas.note:
• Many buildings in Bolivia consist of large red bricks.
  • Buildings often have an ‘unfinished' look.

--- NOTE:

  • This style of architecture is also common in parts of Peru.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Orange Tiled Roofs
metas.note: • Many houses throughout Brazil have orange tiled roofs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Bulgaria - Patches Of Mortar
metas.note:
• Most houses in Bulgaria have orange tiled roofs, with distinct patches of mortar along the corner tiles.

Famously, Bulgarian roofs often seem poorly constructed:

  • The roof tiles and mortar tend to be uneven, especially when compared to other European countries.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bulgaria for more clues.

metas.name: Cambodia - Blue Windows
metas.note:
Traditional Cambodian wooden stilt houses tend to have very recognizable colour schemes:

  • Walls are commonly painted dark red-brown, light blue or an ochre orange.
  • Doors, windows and other architectural details are often painted bright blue.

--- NOTE:

  • More modern houses tend to have a wider variety of colour schemes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/cambodia for more clues.

metas.name: Cambodia - Stilts & Double Roofs
metas.note:
• Wooden houses on stilts are common.
  • Walls are often made of vertical planks.
  • Many homes have double or triple roofs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/cambodia for more clues.

metas.name: Croatia - Adriatic Coast - Beige Bricks
metas.note:
• Houses and walls made of beige brick are common on the Adriatic coast.
  • They often feature green shutters.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar architecture can also be found in some regions in Italy.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Croatia - Red Brick Walls
metas.note:
• Buildings in Croatia sometimes feature exposed red brick walls.
  • This architecture is more common in inland areas.

--- NOTE:

  • This type of architecture can also be found in Slovenia and Serbia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Czechia - Diamond Shaped Tiles
metas.note:
• Roofs with diamond shaped tiles are common in both Czechia and Slovakia.

--- NOTE:

  • This is also somewhat common in Hungary.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/czechia for more clues.

metas.name: Czechia - North - White Stripes
metas.note: • Dark wooden houses, with white stripes shining through the wood, are common in most of northern Czechia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/czechia for more clues.

metas.name: Czechia - Pair Houses
metas.note:
• Suburban houses in Czechia are commonly connected in pairs.

--- NOTE:

  • This is less common in most neighbouring countries, including Slovakia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/czechia for more clues.

metas.name: Denmark - Red Bricks
metas.note:
• Much of the architecture in Denmark consists of red brick.
  • Roofs often have orange, dark brown or black tiles.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar brick architecture is also common in the Netherlands and Belgium.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/denmark for more clues.

metas.name: Ecuador - Grey Bricks
metas.note:
• Most houses are made of grey bricks and have metal roofs.

--- NOTE:

  • This is not unique to Ecuador, but is very common.
  • Countries such as Peru, and especially Bolivia, commonly use red bricks.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: France - Brittany - Architecture
metas.note:
• Brittany has one of the most recognizable and consistent architectures in the country.
  • Common elements include, in addition to black roofs, edge chimneys, black slate walls and stones surrounding doors and windows.
  • The walls will be either very light coloured or made of stone.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/france for more clues.

metas.name: France - Northwest - Black Shingle Roofs
metas.note:
• Black shingle roofs are primarily found in the northwest, the rough cutoff being the Loire river.
  • Other areas include near the Belgian border, the south-centre, and the Pyrenees, making black roofs a good clue for Alps-Pyrenees toss-ups.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/france for more clues.

metas.name: France - South - Rounded Tiles
metas.note: • Roofs in the south of the country will often be made up of rounded tiles overlapping one another, often varying in colour.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/france for more clues.

metas.name: Germany - Central - Black Fish Scale Roofs & Walls
metas.note: • Houses with black slate walls, resembling fish scales, are commonly found in a large area of central Germany.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/germany for more clues.

metas.name: Germany - East - Large Apartment Buildings
metas.note: • These large, utilitarian apartment buildings constructed during the socialist era, that are also known as “Commie blocks” are common in all of former East Germany.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/germany for more clues.

metas.name: Germany - Northwest - Brick Houses
metas.note:
• These brick houses are generally concentrated in northwestern Germany.

--- NOTE:

  • This map is very approximate.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/germany for more clues.

metas.name: Greece - Cyclade Islands - White Walls & Blue Doors
metas.note:
One of the most well-known types of Greek architecture:

  • Houses with completely white walls, blue doors and shutters, is mainly found on the small central Cyclade islands.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/greece for more clues.

metas.name: Greenland - Colorful Wooden Houses
metas.note:
• Greenlandic architecture mainly consists of small, colourful, simple looking wooden houses, which even in cities are typically placed quite sparsely.
  • The major cities have some larger buildings, which normally look fairly minimalistic.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: India - Central - Rounded Roof Tiles
metas.note:
• Rounded roof tiles are common in central India.
  • They often appear disorganised and are kept in rows/columns that are not completely straight.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - East Coast - Thatched Roofs
metas.note:
• Houses or huts with thatched roofs are mainly found along the east coast and northern plains.
  • Large hay mounds are also generally more common in this region.

--- NOTE:

  • Thatched roofs from Uttar Pradesh to Odisha tend to be made of fine pieces of hay whereas thatched roofs from Odisha to Tamil Nadu tend to be made of dried palm fans.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Northeast - Triangle Metal Roofs
metas.note: • Metal roofs, with a small triangle near the top, are common in Northeast India.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - South - Organized Tiles
metas.note:
• Roofs in southern India are characterised by more organised tiles that are bright orange and flat with a ridge in the middle.
  • It is particularly common in Tamil Nadu.

--- NOTE:

  • Similarly shaped tiles with a darker brown colour are common further north.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: Indonesia - Bali - Architecture
metas.note:
• Architecture in Bali is unique because it was influenced by old Balinese culture and Hinduism.
  • The most important thing to look for are these crown-like roof pinnacles, found everywhere in Bali.
  • Guardian statues and slit-drum towers are common too.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Indonesia - Gable Horns
metas.note:
• Roofs with gable horns can be found most commonly in South Sulawesi, Riau and Central and South Kalimantan.

--- NOTE:

  • Horned roofs are often found with Bugis roofs in South Sulawesi.
  • Use this tip along with other clues to determine which region you are in.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Indonesia - Java - Tiled Roofs
metas.note:
• Tiled roofs are most commonly found on the island of Java, and sometimes nearby regions such as southern Sumatra, the Lesser Sunda Islands, and South Kalimantan.

--- NOTE:

  • The tiles on roofs in South Kalimantan and Jambi look slightly different.
  • The tiles are usually less rounded but flatter.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Indonesia - Kalimantan - Wooden Chips
metas.note: • On Kalimantan, you can find these unique roofs made out of wooden chips.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Indonesia - North - Plain Sheet Metal Roofs
metas.note:
• Plain sheet metal roofs are more commonly found toward the north, where tiled roofs are not found.
  • They are most commonly found on Kalimantan, Sulawesi and Sumatra.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Ireland - Cream Colors & Black Roofs
metas.note:
• You will usually find cream white buildings with black roofs in Ireland.
  • Sometimes, the buildings feature grey corner stones.
  • In cities, you will typically find row buildings.

--- NOTE:

  • British style brick buildings can still be found in Ireland.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ireland for more clues.

metas.name: Isle Of Man - Whitewashed Walls
metas.note: • Houses with whitewashed walls and entrance walls are a common sight, similar to Ireland.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Israel - Blocky Buildings
metas.note:
• Architecture tends to consist of bright and warm-coloured stone buildings, often with a blocky appearance.
  • While Mediterranean-style houses with orange tiled roofs are more common than in other Middle Eastern countries, flat roofs are still just as common.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank for more clues.

metas.name: Italy - Alps - Alpine Architecture
metas.note: • Alpine architecture, which typically features large buildings with white stone walls and wooden details, are found in the Alpine region.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/italy for more clues.

metas.name: Italy - Apulian - Flat Roofs
metas.note:
• Houses in the Apulian region are generally very light coloured, and have flat roofs, typically with two to three floors.
  • The architecture is sometimes reminiscent of the Middle East.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/italy for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - North & South - Roof Transition
metas.note:
• The further you are north, roofs generally transition from tiled to level or flat sloped in order to compensate for heavy snowfall.
  • Northern houses often have ladders attached to the side, giving roof access to clear snow.

--- NOTE:

  • In addition to north to south, high-elevation mountainous regions or high snowfall areas often use such roofs, even in more central or southern prefectures.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Lesotho - Round Huts
metas.note:
• In rural areas, you will often see traditional round huts with thatched roofs.

--- NOTE:

  • These are less common in the other three southern African countries, but can still be seen.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/lesotho for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - East - White Concrete Blocks
metas.note:
• White concrete block buildings are highly concentrated in the states surrounding Mexico city, and are generally more common to the east.
  • They can however still be found all over the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mexico for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - North - American Style Bungalows
metas.note:
• Architecture in northern Mexico often features design elements from American style bungalows.
  • Many houses are coloured with light or pastel colours, gated and commonly have front yards.
  • Orange tiles inspired by Spanish colonial architecture are also typical.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mexico for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - West - Red Bricks
metas.note: • Red brick buildings are mostly concentrated in the states west of Mexico City, specifically Jalisco, Michoacan, Guanajuato, and Aguascalientes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mexico for more clues.

metas.name: Netherlands - Red-Brownish Bricks
metas.note:
• Brick architecture is very common in the Netherlands.
  • Many buildings feature red-brownish-coloured bricks.
  • Roofs often have orange or dark grey tiles.

--- NOTE:

  • Similar brick architecture is also common in Denmark and Belgium.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/netherlands for more clues.

metas.name: Netherlands - South - Rolling Shutters
metas.note:
• Rolling shutters on house windows are more common in the southern half of the Netherlands.

--- NOTE:

  • While more prevalent in the south, rolling shutters on homes in more northern regions are not unheard of.
  • Use this meta with some caution.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/netherlands for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - North - Overhanging Roofs
metas.note:
• Buildings with overhanging roofs with wooden supports are mostly found in northern regions of Peru.
  • These buildings are sometimes brightly coloured as well.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - South - Red Brick Transition
metas.note:
• As a general rule, the closer you are to Lake Titicaca in Peru, houses and buildings made out of red brick become more common.
  • This type of architecture resembles the predominant type of building seen in parts of western Bolivia, which is helpful for remembering where it is seen most commonly.

--- NOTE:

  • Red brick buildings can be seen anywhere in the country, so use other clues before guessing.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - South - Diamond Pattern
metas.note: • Houses built with amakan walls, a traditionally woven bamboo mat, with a diamond pattern are almost exclusively found in the southern half of the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Portugal - White Stone & Orange Roofs
metas.note: • White painted stone houses with orange tiled roofs are extremely common in Portugal.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/portugal for more clues.

metas.name: Romania - East - Metal & Fake Tiled Roofs
metas.note: • If you see several houses and almost all of them have metal or plastic fake tiled roofs, you will probably be in the eastern half of the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/romania for more clues.

metas.name: Romania - West - Orange Tiled Roofs
metas.note: • If you see several houses and almost all of them have orange tiled roofs, you are likely to be in the western half of the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/romania for more clues.

metas.name: Russia - Decorated Window Frames
metas.note:
• This style of richly decorated window frames is commonly found on traditional Russian homes, especially on log cabins.
  • They are often painted blue.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/russia for more clues.

metas.name: Slovakia - East - Grey Metal Roofs
metas.note:
• Grey metal roofs are very common, particularly in the eastern parts of Slovakia.

--- NOTE:

  • Apart from the most mountainous areas, it is far less common in Czechia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/slovakia for more clues.

metas.name: Slovenia - Alpine Architecture
metas.note:
• Slovenian architecture takes much inspiration from alpine architecture, with light coloured walls, dark wooden details and semi-steep roofs.
  • The most common roof shape is half-hipped roofs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/slovenia for more clues.

metas.name: Spain - Catalonia & Aragón - Masias
metas.note:
• Traditional farm houses called “masías” are common in Catalonia, eastern Aragón and parts of the Valencian Community.
  • They are usually made of stone and stand isolated or as part of a small complex.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/spain for more clues.

metas.name: Spain - Centre & South - White Towns
metas.note:
• Within the centre and south of Spain, towns made completely out of white painted houses are very common in Andalucía and Extremadura.
  • You can still see a fair amount of white painted houses in Castilla la Mancha but streets where every house is white will not be common.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/spain for more clues.

metas.name: Spain - Northwest - Slate Roofs
metas.note:
• There is a large part of north-west Spain where you will find almost exclusively slate roofs (recognisable by their almost black colour).
  • This type of roofing can be seen sparingly all the way to the west coast of Galicia, but ends rather abruptly on the east.

--- NOTE:

  • Slate roofs can also be found in the Pyrenees near Andorra, and in the mountain ranges north east of Madrid.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/spain for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Grey Metal Roofs
metas.note:
• Grey metal roofs on residential buildings generally get more common the further north in the country you get.
  • Note that metal roofs on barns and sheds can be found significantly further south.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Skåne - Colored Triangle
metas.note:
• Houses in Skåne commonly have either a white stone, or a red brick wall with a coloured wooden triangle beneath the roof on the sides.
  • Similar houses with other materials (such as grey brick) for the walls can be found elsewhere in the southern half of the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Switzerland - Bern - Arch Shapes
metas.note: • Large houses with thick roofs, which are shaped like an arch underneath, are common around Bern.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/switzerland for more clues.

metas.name: Switzerland - Graubünden - Decorative Details
metas.note: • In the canton of Graubünden, you will often come across houses entirely made of stone, with, most commonly white, decorative painted details around windows and the edges of the house.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/switzerland for more clues.

metas.name: Taiwan - Kinmen - Traditional Architecture
metas.note: • You can find these small, traditional-looking houses in Kinmen.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/taiwan for more clues.

metas.name: Taiwan - North - Old & Disorganized Buildings
metas.note: • Old and disorganised housing units as well as tall dingy-looking apartment blocks are frequently seen in the urban areas of northern Taiwan.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/taiwan for more clues.

metas.name: Taiwan - Yilan - Multiple-Story Villas
metas.note:
• In Yilan, you can find these rich multiple-story villas.
  • They come in all types of designs and are often gated.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/taiwan for more clues.

metas.name: Thailand - Corrugated Metal Roofs
metas.note: • Gray corrugated metal roofs are most commonly found in the north and south of the country, but can occasionally be found throughout the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/thailand for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - Batman - Spherical Water Tanks
metas.note: • White spherical water tanks can be found in the southeast, mainly south of Batman.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - East - Metal Roofs
metas.note: • Metal roofs are most common in the east.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - South Coast - Flat Roofs
metas.note: • Flat roofs are mostly found in the southeast and to a lesser extent along the south coast.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - West - Tiled Roofs
metas.note:
• Tiled roofs are mostly found in the western two thirds of the country.
  • Note that for this and the following roof-related tips to be reliable, the majority of all visible roofs should preferably be of that type.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Identical Look
metas.note:
• Suburbs in UK towns tend to have a recognizable look.
  • They typically feature near-identical houses, often semi-detached, usually with well-manicured lawns.
  • The road layout can be maze-like, with lots of cul-de-sacs and curvy roads.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom for more clues.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Scotland - Sandstone & Granite
metas.note:
• It is common to see houses made of large blocks of sandstone or granite in Scotland.
  • Granite buildings are common in Aberdeen, red sandstone is common in Glasgow and Dumfries, and yellow sandstone is common in Edinburgh.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom for more clues.
